title: Effects of Whole-Body Vibrations on Neuromuscular Fatigue
author: Milos Kalc
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.beadjaa6
materials: Repete assessment procedure go to step #8

steps.title: Warm‑up bench stepping
steps.instruction: Perform a 6‑minute warm‑up by bench stepping on a 20 cm high step at 0.5 Hz, exchanging the stepping leg each minute.

steps.title: Calibrate isometric dynamometer
steps.instruction: Before each measuring session, calibrate the custom‑made isometric dynamometer (force transducer MES, Maribor, Slovenia) by hanging a 20 kg weight, recording the voltage output with the PowerLab 16/35 DAQ (ADInstruments) running LabChart 7 on Windows XP, and compute the torque conversion factor.

steps.title: Seat subject on dynamometer
steps.instruction: Seat the participant upright on the dynamometer, set trunk lean to 100°, secure pelvis with straps and a horizontal pad over the distal third of the thigh, align the knee joint axis with the machine axis, place the shin pad just above the medial malleolus, and fix the right knee at 60° flexion (0° = full extension).

steps.title: Place femoral nerve electrodes
steps.instruction: With the subject seated and hip flexed, palpate the iliac fossa and femoral triangle; insert a 10 mm Ag–AgCl cathode (type 0601000402, Controle Graphique Medical) into the femoral triangle and place a larger self‑adhesive 50 × 100 mm anode (Compex) over the gluteal fold.

steps.title: Test stimulation site
steps.instruction: Deliver single square‑wave pulses (1 ms duration) from a Digitimer DS7A constant‑current stimulator at 20 mA and 0.1 Hz, applying 3 ± impulses (up to 6) while slightly moving the cathode to locate the spot that yields the highest knee‑extensor torque.

steps.title: Determine supra‑maximal intensity
steps.instruction: After the warm‑up, start stimulation at 10 mA and increase by 10 mA increments until torque no longer rises with higher current; then multiply the current that produced maximal twitch torque by 1.5 to obtain a supra‑maximal stimulus, and keep this intensity for the whole session.

steps.title: Record MVC with double‑twitch interpolation
steps.instruction: Ask the subject to perform a 5‑second maximal isometric knee‑extension (MVC); smooth the torque signal with a 0.5 s moving‑average window and record the peak MVC torque. Superimpose a 100 Hz doublet (T_MVC) on the MVC plateau, wait 3 s, then deliver a second 100 Hz doublet (T_100) to the relaxed muscle. Calculate voluntary activation (%VA) as %VA = (1 − (T_MVC − MVC)/T_100) × 100.

steps.title: High‑ and low‑frequency doublet measurements
steps.instruction: Apply paired supramaximal doublets: a high‑frequency doublet at 100 Hz (10 ms inter‑stimulus interval) and a low‑frequency doublet at 20 Hz (50 ms interval). Record peak torque for each (T_100 and T_20) and compute the low‑to‑high frequency ratio as T_20/100 = (T_20 / T_100) × 100.

steps.title: Single‑twitch torque measurement
steps.instruction: Deliver a single supramaximal femoral‑nerve stimulus and record the resulting torque; note the maximum torque value (TW_PT).

steps.title: Whole‑body vibration intervention
steps.instruction: Place the subject on a Galileo Fit whole‑body vibration platform (Novotec Medical) set to 26 Hz (or off for SHAM). Instruct the subject to maintain a half‑squat with knees at 60°, feet 40 cm apart, while the platform produces a peak‑to‑peak displacement amplitude of 5 mm.
